note: The closed vocabulary of a proof, and the ONLY place a proof kind is declared. scripts/proofs.py loads this file and refuses a kind it does not find here; tests/test_proofs.py asserts the registry and this file agree in both directions. Adding a kind is therefore a two-file change with a test that fails until both exist.

control.description: Optional. A second proof that the orchestrator runs and requires to be REFUTED, on the same or another kind. It is the claim's negative control: evidence that the check is capable of failing. A blocking claim without one is `uncontrolled` — admissible as a note, never as a defect.

absent.description: No file in the tree matches `pattern` outside `exclude`. Proves dead code, an absent call site, a removed identifier.

pattern.description: Python regex, searched line by line.

include.description: fnmatch globs on the POSIX relative path.

max_files.description: Above this the proof is unrunnable, never silently truncated.

present.description: A cited line exists and says what was claimed. Proves a citation, kills a hallucinated one.

text.description: Substring that must appear in the cited lines.

command.description: A command's exit status or output proves the claim. Proves a test fails, a build breaks, an analyzer hits.

argv.description: Executable first, no shell, no string concatenation.

dom.description: A page, loaded in a headless browser, contains or lacks an element. Proves runtime behaviour rather than source.

url.description: Defaults to $COUNCIL_WEB_URL or the first web entry point.

http.description: A LOCAL endpoint answers as claimed. Proves an API contract; refuses any non-loopback host, because a proof that reaches the network is not reproducible.

json.description: A structured file holds a value at a pointer. Proves manifest, config and lockfile claims without reading prose.

equals.description: Value the pointer must hold. Omit only with `absent: true`.

diff.description: A line is part of this change, or was removed by it. Proves a defect is new rather than inherited.
